extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, petitioners, patent owners, and counsel practicing before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing trials and preliminary proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), including filing, service, motions, evidence standards, counsel rules, fees, and sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of settlement agreements (constructive notice / timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 135(c), an agreement or understanding, including collateral agreements made in connection with or in contemplation of the termination of an interference must be filed prior to the termination of the interference between the parties to the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a final decision is entered, an interference is terminated when no appeal (35 U.S.C. 141) or other review (35 U.S.C. 146) has been or can be taken. If an appeal or civil action has been filed, the interference is considered terminated when that appeal or action is terminated (e.g., when mandate issued or time to appeal expires).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of order of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are presumed to have invented interfering subject matter in the order of the dates of their accorded benefit for each count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two parties are accorded the benefit of the same earliest constructive reduction to practice date, then neither party is entitled to a presumption of priority over the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standard for priority
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority may be proved by a preponderance of the evidence except where a different standard applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party must prove priority by clear and convincing evidence if the date of its earliest constructive reduction to practice is after the issue date of an involved patent or the publication date under 35 U.S.C. 122(b) of an involved application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim correspondence presumption
rubrics_metrics.description: For determining priority and derivation, all claims of a party corresponding to the count are presumed to stand or fall together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To challenge this presumption, a party must file a timely substantive motion to have a corresponding claim designated as not corresponding to the count. No presumption based on claim correspondence exists for other grounds of unpatentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of when a claim corresponds to a count
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim corresponds to a count if the subject matter of the count, treated as prior art to the claim, would have anticipated or rendered obvious the subject matter of the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-applicability of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: When a motion for judgment of unpatentability against an opponent’s claim on the basis of prior art is granted, each of the movant’s claims corresponding to the same count as the opponent’s claim will be presumed to be unpatentable in view of the same prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The movant may rebut this presumption in its motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and permissible subjects of substantive motions in an interference
rubrics_metrics.description: In an interference, substantive motions must: (1) raise a threshold issue; (2) seek to change the scope of the definition of the interfering subject matter or the correspondence of claims to the count; (3) seek to change the benefit accorded for the count; or (4) seek judgment on derivation or on priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions must provide a showing, supported with appropriate evidence, such that, if unrebutted, it would justify the relief sought; the burden of proof is on the movant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing patentability for added/amended claims or counts
rubrics_metrics.description: A party moving to add or amend a claim must show the claim is patentable; a party moving to add or amend a count must show the count is patentable over prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Part 42 (construction and incorporated rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 42 governs proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board; sections of part 1 also apply as incorporated. This part shall be construed to secure the just, speedy, and inexpensive resolution of every proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decorum requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every party must act with courtesy and decorum in all proceedings before the Board, including in interactions with other parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default evidentiary standard in Part 42 proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The default evidentiary standard is a preponderance of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of key terms used in Part 42
rubrics_metrics.description: Part 42 provides definitions for terms such as Affidavit, Board, Business day, Confidential information, Final, Hearing, Involved, Judgment, Motion, Office, Panel, Party, Petition, Petitioner, Preliminary Proceeding, Proceeding, Rehearing, and Trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions govern construction of the rules in Part 42 (e.g., what constitutes a 'trial' vs. an interference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may exercise exclusive jurisdiction within the Office over every involved application and patent during the proceeding, as the Board may order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition to institute a trial must be filed with the Board consistent with any time period required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of trial / institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board institutes the trial on behalf of the Director and will send notice of a trial to every party to the proceeding; the entry of the notice institutes the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may authorize additional modes of notice, including sending notice to another address associated with the party or publishing the notice in the Official Gazette or Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board control over conduct of proceeding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may determine a proper course of conduct for any situation not specifically covered and may enter non-final orders to administer the proceeding; the Board may waive or suspend requirements of parts 1, 41, and 42 and place conditions on waivers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Times set by rule are default and may be modified by order. A request for extension of time must be supported by a showing of good cause. Late action will be excused on showing of good cause or if consideration on the merits would be in the interests of justice. Ex parte communications with a Board member are not permitted unless both parties have an opportunity to be involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format requirements for documents and exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Page size must be 8.5 inch × 11 inch (except exhibits requiring larger size). Markings must be black or equivalent high-contrast; 14-point Times New Roman proportional font with normal spacing; double spacing except in claim charts, headings, tables, indices, signature blocks, and certificates of service; margins at least 2.5 cm (1 inch) on all sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Block quotations may be 1.5 spaced and indented. Arguments must not be incorporated by reference from one document into another. Combined motions/oppositions/replies or other combined documents are not permitted. Documents must be signed per §§ 1.33 and 11.18(a) and should be identified by trial number where known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of filing (electronic preferred) and non-electronic filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise authorized, submissions are to be made electronically via the Internet per Board parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-electronic filing must be accompanied by a motion requesting acceptance and identify a date of transmission if seeking a filing date other than date of receipt. For exhibits filed separately, a transmittal letter with certificate of service is required stating name and exhibit number(s). The certificate of service must state the date and manner of service and the name and address of every person served. Mailed correspondence address is provided (Mail Stop PATENT BOARD...).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit filing timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each exhibit must be filed with the first document in which it is cited, except as the Board may otherwise order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously filed paper restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: A document already in the record of the proceeding must not be filed again, not even as an exhibit or appendix, without express Board authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service rules (methods, timing, certificate of service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Service may be electronic upon agreement; otherwise service must be by Priority Mail Express® or means at least as fast and reliable. Each document filed with the Board, if not previously served, must be served simultaneously on each opposing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If party is represented, service must be on counsel. Each document (other than an exhibit) must include a certificate of service at the end naming the date and manner of service and persons served. For exhibits filed with documents, the exhibit may be included in the certification for the document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management of the record (expungement and stay of non-Board actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may expunge any paper directed to a proceeding or filed while an application or patent is under Board jurisdiction that is not authorized under this part or a Board order, or that is filed contrary to a Board order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may vacate or hold in abeyance any non-Board action directed to a proceeding while the application or patent is under Board jurisdiction unless authorized by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notices (real party-in-interest, related matters, counsel, service info)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain notices must be filed with the Board: by the petitioner as part of the petition; by the patent owner (or applicant in derivation) within 21 days of service of the petition; or by either party within 21 days of a change of information previously filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices required include identification of each real party-in-interest; identification of related judicial/administrative matters; identification of lead and back-up counsel; service information (email, postal, hand-delivery address, telephone, facsimile). A power of attorney must be filed with designation of counsel when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner action (entire vs part interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner of the entire interest in an involved application or patent may act to the exclusion of the inventor. An owner of a part interest may move to act to the exclusion of an inventor or co-owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A motion by part owner must show inability or refusal of an inventor or co-owner to prosecute or other cause demonstrating it is in the interests of justice; Board may set conditions on actions of parties if motion granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counsel designation and backup; exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party is represented by counsel, the party must designate lead counsel and at least one back-up counsel who can conduct business on behalf of lead counsel. Lead counsel must be a registered practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may permit a party to proceed without back-up counsel upon a showing of good cause (e.g., lack of financial resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro hac vice admission and provisionally recognized PTAB attorneys
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may recognize counsel pro hac vice upon a showing of good cause and subject to condition that lead counsel be a registered practitioner. Provisionally recognized PTAB attorneys (previously admitted pro hac vice and not subsequently denied) may be eligible for automatic pro hac vice admission subject to specified procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include filing a notice of intent to designate provisionally recognized attorney as back-up counsel, identifying registered practitioner who will serve as lead counsel, submitting a certification/declaration, 5-business-day objection window, and deemed admission if no timely objection or Board order. If unable to satisfy requirements, pro hac vice admission must be sought via standard process. Provisionally recognized attorneys have a continuing duty to notify the Board within 5 business days of sanctions, suspension, disbarment, loss of good standing, or other material changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification and withdrawal of counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel of the Board may disqualify counsel for cause after notice and opportunity for hearing. Counsel may not withdraw from a proceeding before the Board unless the Board authorizes such withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A decision to disqualify is not final for judicial review until certified by the Chief Administrative Patent Judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor, signature, and representations
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties and individuals have a duty of candor and good faith to the Office during the proceeding. Every petition, response, written motion, and other paper must comply with signature requirements in § 11.18(a). By presenting papers to the Board an attorney, registered practitioner, or unrepresented party attests to compliance with certification requirements under § 11.18(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may expunge unsigned submissions unless omission is promptly corrected after being called to attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: initiation, motion procedure, and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board determines that representations to the Board (e.g., certification under § 11.18(b)(2)) have been violated, it may impose an appropriate sanction. A motion for sanctions must be made separately, describe the specific conduct, be authorized by the Board under § 42.20 prior to filing, and the moving party must serve the other party at least 21 days prior to seeking authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A motion for sanctions must not be filed if the challenged paper/claim/defense is withdrawn or corrected within 21 days after service (or other time set by Board). Board may award reasonable expenses, including attorney’s fees, for the motion if warranted. On its own initiative, the Board may order a show-cause and impose sanctions; sanctions must be limited to what suffices to deter repetition and consistent with § 42.12. An order imposing a sanction must describe the sanctioned conduct and explain the basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions: grounds and possible sanctions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may impose sanctions for misconduct including failure to comply with rules or orders, advancing misleading or frivolous arguments, misrepresentation of fact, engaging in dilatory tactics, abuse of discovery, abuse of process, or other improper use of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctions may include holding facts established, expunging or precluding filing a paper, precluding presentation/contest of an issue, precluding discovery requests/obtainment/opposition, excluding evidence, awarding compensatory expenses (including attorney fees), requiring terminal disclaimer of patent term, or judgment/dismissal of petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of authority requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For any U.S. Supreme Court decision, citation to the United States Reports is preferred; for other decisions, citation to the West Reporter System is preferred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations must include pinpoint citations when specific holdings/portions are invoked. Non-binding authority should be used sparingly; if the authority is not Office authority and not reproduced in U.S. Reports or West, provide a copy of the authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and sealing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of a proceeding, including documents and things, shall be made available to the public except as otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party intending to seal must file a motion to seal concurrent with the filing of the document/thing to be sealed; the document/thing shall be provisionally sealed on receipt of the motion pending decision on the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees required for filing petitions and related requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific fees are due when filing petitions for inter partes review, post-grant review, covered business method review, derivation proceedings, and for certain other requests (e.g., making a settlement agreement available, pro hac vice appearance fee, Director review).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are set by rule (examples include request and post-institution fees for IPR and PGR; additional per-claim fees for claims over 20; derivation petition fee; fee for counsel not registered to appear pro hac vice; fee for Director review). (The rule text lists the amounts and the circumstances under which each fee is required.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of relief and motion authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Relief other than a petition requesting institution of a trial must be requested in the form of a motion. A motion will not be entered without Board authorization (which may be provided in an order of general applicability or during the proceeding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The moving party has the burden of proof to establish entitlement to requested relief. The Board may order briefing on any issue involved in the trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of basis for relief (notice content and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may require a party to file a notice stating the relief it requests and the basis for its entitlement. A notice must include sufficient detail to place the Board and each opponent on notice of the precise relief requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A notice is not evidence except as an admission by a party-opponent. The Board may set times/conditions for filing and may keep the notice confidential for a limited time. Failure to state a sufficient basis may result in denial, a party will be limited to filing motions consistent with the notice, and ambiguities in the notice will be construed against the party. A party may move to correct its notice promptly; late corrections entered only if in the interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for petitions and motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each petition or motion must be filed as a separate paper and must include (1) a statement of the precise relief requested, and (2) a full statement of the reasons for the relief requested, including a detailed explanation of the significance of the evidence including material facts, and the governing law, rules, and precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a rule in part 1 ordinarily governs the relief sought, the petition or motion must make any required showings under that rule in addition to Part 42 showings. Each petition or motion may include a statement of material fact, preferably set forth as separately numbered sentences with specific citations to the record. The Board may order additional showings/explanations as a condition for authorizing a motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions, replies, and sur-replies content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppositions, replies, and sur-replies must comply with the content requirements for motions. If the paper responded to contains a statement of material fact, the response must include a listing of facts that are admitted, denied, or cannot be admitted or denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material fact not specifically denied may be considered admitted. All arguments for relief requested must be made in the motion; a reply may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding opposition, preliminary response, response, or decision on institution. A sur-reply may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding reply and may not be accompanied by new evidence other than deposition transcripts of cross-examination of any reply witness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type-volume and page limits for petitions, motions, oppositions, replies, and sur-replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified word counts/page limits apply: Petition requesting inter partes review: 14,000 words; Petition requesting post-grant review: 18,700 words; Petition requesting covered business method review: 18,700 words; Petition requesting derivation proceeding: 14,000 words. Motions (excluding motions to amend): 15 pages. Motions to amend: 25 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Word counts/pages include any statement of material facts but exclude table of contents, table of authorities, mandatory notices under § 42.8, certificate of service or word count, and appendix of exhibits/claim listing. Petitions to institute a trial may be accompanied by a motion to waive word counts; the petitioner must show how a waiver serves the interests of justice and append the proposed overlong petition. If the motion to waive is not granted, the proposed overlong petition may be expunged or returned. Other waiver motions must be granted in advance of filing the affected paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner responses and oppositions word counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Word counts or page limits for patent owner preliminary responses and responses to petitions are the same as the word counts for the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word counts for these responses do not include a listing of facts which are admitted, denied, or cannot be admitted or denied. Papers must include a certification stating the number of words (a party may rely on the word count of the word-processing system used).
